heading: Short title, extent and commencement.
text: (1) This Act may be called the Sexual Harassment of Women at Workplace (Prevention, Prohibition and Redressal) Act, 2013. (2) It extends to the whole of India. (3) It shall come into force on such date as the Central Government may, by notification in the Official Gazette, appoint.[cite: 1]

heading: Definitions.
text: Provides definitions for key terms used in the Act, including aggrieved woman, appropriate Government, Chairperson, District Officer, domestic worker, employee, employer, Internal Committee, Local Committee, Member, prescribed, Presiding Officer, respondent, sexual harassment, workplace, and unorganised sector.[cite: 1]

heading: Prevention of sexual harassment.
text: (1) No woman shall be subjected to sexual harassment at any workplace. (2) The following circumstances, among other circumstances, if it occurs, or is present in relation to or connected with any act or behavior of sexual harassment may amount to sexual harassment:- (i) implied or explicit promise of preferential treatment in her employment; or (ii) implied or explicit threat of detrimental treatment in her employment; or (iii) implied or explicit threat about her present or future employment status; or (iv) interference with her work or creating an intimidating or offensive or hostile work environment for her; or (v) humiliating treatment likely to affect her health or safety.[cite: 1]

heading: Constitution of Internal Complaints Committee.
text: Every employer of a workplace shall, by an order in writing, constitute a Committee to be known as the Internal Complaints Committee. The Internal Committees shall consist of a Presiding Officer, not less than two Members from amongst employees, and one member from amongst non-governmental organisations. The Presiding Officer and Members hold office for a period not exceeding three years.[cite: 1]

heading: Notification of District Officer.
text: The appropriate Government may notify a District Magistrate or Additional District Magistrate or the Collector or Deputy Collector as a District Officer for every District to exercise powers or discharge functions under this Act.[cite: 1]

heading: Constitution and jurisdiction of Local Committee.
text: Every District Officer shall constitute in the district concerned, a committee to be known as the Local Committee to receive complaints of sexual harassment from establishments where the Internal Committee has not been constituted due to having less than ten workers or if the complaint is against the employer himself.[cite: 1]

heading: Composition, tenure and other terms and conditions of Local Committee.
text: The Local Committee shall consist of a Chairperson nominated from amongst eminent women in social work, one Member from working women in the district, two Members from non-governmental organisations committed to the cause of women, and the concerned officer dealing with social welfare as an ex officio member. Members hold office for up to three years.[cite: 1]

heading: Grants and audit.
text: The Central Government may make grants to the State Government for payment of fees or allowances for the Local Committee. The State Government may set up an agency to transfer and audit these funds.[cite: 1]

heading: Complaint of sexual harassment.
text: Any aggrieved woman may make, in writing, a complaint of sexual harassment at workplace to the Internal Committee or Local Committee within a period of three months from the date of incident. Where she is unable to make a complaint, her legal heir or prescribed person may do so.[cite: 1]

heading: Conciliation.
text: The Committee may, before initiating an inquiry and at the request of the aggrieved woman, take steps to settle the matter between her and the respondent through conciliation, provided no monetary settlement shall be made as a basis of conciliation.[cite: 1]

heading: Inquiry into complaint.
text: The Committee shall proceed to make inquiry into the complaint in accordance with the provisions of the service rules applicable to the respondent. The Committee shall have the same powers as a civil court under the Code of Civil Procedure, 1908, when trying a suit. The inquiry shall be completed within a period of ninety days.[cite: 1]

heading: Action during pendency of inquiry.
text: During pendency of an inquiry, the Committee may recommend to the employer to transfer the aggrieved woman or respondent, grant leave to the aggrieved woman up to three months, or grant other relief.[cite: 1]

heading: Inquiry report.
text: On completion of an inquiry, the Committee shall provide a report of its findings to the employer or District Officer within ten days. If the allegation is proved, they recommend action for sexual harassment as misconduct and deduction of appropriate compensation from the respondent's salary.[cite: 1]

heading: Punishment for false or malicious complaint and false evidence.
text: Where the Committee concludes that the allegation is malicious, the complaint is known to be false, or forged documents were produced, it may recommend action against the complainant or witness.[cite: 1]

heading: Determination of compensation.
text: Compensation to the aggrieved woman shall have regard to mental trauma, pain, loss of career opportunity, medical expenses, income and financial status of the respondent, and feasibility of payment.[cite: 1]

heading: Prohibition of publication or making known contents of complaint and inquiry proceedings.
text: The contents of the complaint, identity and addresses of the aggrieved woman, respondent, and witnesses, and inquiry proceedings shall not be published, communicated or made known to the public, press and media in any manner.[cite: 1]

heading: Penalty for publication or making known contents of complaint and inquiry proceedings.
text: Any person contravening section 16 shall be liable for penalty in accordance with the provisions of their service rules or as prescribed.[cite: 1]

heading: Appeal.
text: Any person aggrieved from the recommendations or non-implementation may prefer an appeal to the court or tribunal within ninety days of the recommendations.[cite: 1]

heading: Duties of employer.
text: Every employer shall provide a safe working environment, display penal consequences of sexual harassment, organise workshops, provide facilities for the Committee, assist in securing attendance of witnesses, and treat sexual harassment as misconduct.[cite: 1]

heading: Duties and powers of District Officer.
text: The District Officer shall monitor the timely submission of reports by the Local Committee and engage non-governmental organisations for awareness creation.[cite: 1]

heading: Committee to submit annual report.
text: The Internal Committee or Local Committee shall in each calendar year prepare and submit an annual report to the employer and District Officer.[cite: 1]

heading: Employer to include information in annual report.
text: The employer shall include in its report the number of cases filed and their disposal under this Act in the annual report of his organisation.[cite: 1]

heading: Appropriate Government to monitor implementation and maintain data.
text: The appropriate Government shall monitor the implementation of this Act and maintain data on the number of cases filed and disposed of.[cite: 1]

heading: Appropriate Government to take measures to publicise the Act.
text: The appropriate Government may develop information, education, communication and training materials, organise awareness programmes, and formulate orientation for Local Committee members.[cite: 1]

heading: Power to call for information and inspection of records.
text: The appropriate Government may call upon any employer or District Officer to furnish information relating to sexual harassment and authorise officers to inspect records.[cite: 1]

heading: Penalty for non-compliance with provisions of Act.
text: Where the employer fails to constitute an Internal Committee, take action under sections 13, 14, and 22, or contravenes other provisions, he shall be punishable with fine extending to fifty thousand rupees. Repeat offenses double the punishment or result in cancellation of licenses.[cite: 1]

heading: Cognizance of offence by courts.
text: No court shall take cognizance of any offence save on a complaint made by the aggrieved woman or authorised person. No court inferior to a Metropolitan Magistrate or Judicial Magistrate first class shall try any offence. Offences are non-cognizable.[cite: 1]

heading: Act not in derogation of any other law.
text: The provisions of this Act shall be in addition to and not in derogation of the provisions of any other law for the time being in force.[cite: 1]

heading: Power of appropriate Government to make rules.
text: The Central Government may, by notification in the Official Gazette, make rules for carrying out the provisions of this Act, subject to approval by Parliament.[cite: 1]

heading: Power to remove difficulties.
text: If any difficulty arises in giving effect to the provisions of this Act, the Central Government may make orders not inconsistent with the Act to remove the difficulty, within two years of commencement.[cite: 1]
